Minimize an R function with OptimLib

Source: R/optimlib.R
optimlib.Rd

A general interface to OptimLib's unconstrained and box-constrained minimizers, modelled on stats::optim(). The objective (and gradient / Hessian, if supplied) are plain R functions called from C++.

Usage

optimlib(
  par,
  fn,
  gr = NULL,
  ...,
  method = c("bfgs", "lbfgs", "cg", "gd", "newton", "nm", "de", "de_prmm", "pso",
    "pso_dv"),
  lower = -Inf,
  upper = Inf,
  hess = NULL,
  control = list()
)

Arguments

par

Numeric vector of starting values.

fn

Objective function to minimize. Called as fn(par, ...) and must return a single number.

gr

Gradient of fn, called as gr(par, ...) and returning a numeric vector of length length(par). If NULL, gradient-based methods use central finite differences. Ignored by derivative-free methods.

...

Further arguments passed to fn, gr and hess.

method

The algorithm:

  • "bfgs": BFGS quasi-Newton.

  • "lbfgs": limited-memory BFGS, for many parameters.

  • "cg": nonlinear conjugate gradient.

  • "gd": gradient descent, including momentum, Nesterov, AdaGrad, RMSProp, AdaDelta, Adam and Nadam variants (see gd$method in optimlib_control()).

  • "newton": Newton's method; uses hess. Does not support bounds.

  • "nm": Nelder-Mead (derivative-free).

  • "de", "de_prmm": differential evolution, and its variant with population reduction and multiple mutation strategies (derivative-free, global).

  • "pso", "pso_dv": particle swarm optimization, and its differentially perturbed velocity variant (derivative-free, global).

lower, upper

Bounds on the parameters, recycled to length(par). Use -Inf / Inf for unbounded parameters. OptimLib handles bounds by transforming the parameters, so par must lie strictly inside them.

hess

Hessian of fn for method = "newton", called as hess(par, ...) and returning a length(par) x length(par) matrix. If NULL, it is approximated by finite differences of the gradient.

control

A list of settings, or the result of optimlib_control().

Value

A list with elements:

  • par: the best parameter values found.

  • value: fn evaluated at par.

  • success: TRUE if OptimLib reports convergence. For the population methods this is only meaningful when check_freq (in de / pso of optimlib_control()) is finite: with the default check_freq = Inf no convergence test is run, and OptimLib reports TRUE for "de" but FALSE for "de_prmm", "pso" and "pso_dv" after n_gen generations. Judge those results by value.

  • iterations: number of iterations (generations for population methods).

  • error: the final value of the convergence criterion.

  • method: the method used.

See also

optimlib_control(), optimlib_sumt() for nonlinear inequality constraints, optimlib_root() for systems of equations.

Examples

rosenbrock <- function(x) 100 * (x[2] - x[1]^2)^2 + (1 - x[1])^2
rosenbrock_gr <- function(x) c(
  -400 * x[1] * (x[2] - x[1]^2) - 2 * (1 - x[1]),
   200 * (x[2] - x[1]^2))

optimlib(c(-1.2, 1), rosenbrock, rosenbrock_gr)
#> $par
#> [1] 1 1
#> 
#> $value
#> [1] 2.233623e-18
#> 
#> $success
#> [1] TRUE
#> 
#> $iterations
#> [1] 31
#> 
#> $error
#> [1] 4.734761e-09
#> 
#> $method
#> [1] "bfgs"
#> 
optimlib(c(-1.2, 1), rosenbrock, rosenbrock_gr, method = "lbfgs")
#> $par
#> [1] 1 1
#> 
#> $value
#> [1] 9.268971e-22
#> 
#> $success
#> [1] TRUE
#> 
#> $iterations
#> [1] 36
#> 
#> $error
#> [1] 1.067933e-09
#> 
#> $method
#> [1] "lbfgs"
#> 
optimlib(c(-1.2, 1), rosenbrock, method = "nm")
#> $par
#> [1] 1 1
#> 
#> $value
#> [1] 3.083427e-14
#> 
#> $success
#> [1] TRUE
#> 
#> $iterations
#> [1] 101
#> 
#> $error
#> [1] 6.647596e-09
#> 
#> $method
#> [1] "nm"
#> 

# Box constraints
optimlib(c(0.5, 0.5), rosenbrock, rosenbrock_gr, lower = 0, upper = 0.8)
#> $par
#> [1] 0.80 0.64
#> 
#> $value
#> [1] 0.04
#> 
#> $success
#> [1] TRUE
#> 
#> $iterations
#> [1] 44
#> 
#> $error
#> [1] 8.949664e-09
#> 
#> $method
#> [1] "bfgs"
#> 

# Global optimization; set.seed() makes the result reproducible
set.seed(2861)
optimlib(c(1, 1), function(x) sum(x^2), method = "de",
         lower = -5, upper = 5, control = list(de = list(n_gen = 200)))
#> $par
#> [1] 0 0
#> 
#> $value
#> [1] 0
#> 
#> $success
#> [1] TRUE
#> 
#> $iterations
#> [1] 201
#> 
#> $error
#> [1] 2e-08
#> 
#> $method
#> [1] "de"
#>
